title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 11
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Forecast and actual sales, in units, at five stores:

Alderby: forecast 480, actual 432
Bracewell: forecast 1,250, actual 1,100
Colford: forecast 320, actual 272
Deeping: forecast 900, actual 846
Elmore: forecast 610, actual 561

Which store missed its forecast by the largest percentage?
options: A. Alderby
B. Bracewell
C. Colford
D. Deeping
E. Elmore
questions.explanation: Shortfall as a percentage of forecast: Alderby 10.0%, Bracewell 12.0%, Colford 15.0%, Deeping 6.0%, Elmore 8.0%. Colford is worst, on the smallest forecast in the table. Bracewell is 150 units short, more than any other store, but against a forecast several times larger.

questions.prompt:
Units produced each month:

Jan: 180
Feb: 165
Mar: 210
Apr: 195
May: 240
Jun: 220

In which month does the running total for the year first pass 1,000 units?
options: A. March
B. April
C. May
D. The running total never passes 1,000
E. June
questions.explanation: Running totals: Jan 180, Feb 345, Mar 555, Apr 750, May 990, Jun 1,210. May ends on 990, ten units short, so the total does not pass 1,000 until Jun.

questions.prompt:
Advertising spend and enquiries, by month:

Jan: GBP 4,000.00 spent, 210 enquiries
Feb: GBP 3,000.00 spent, 190 enquiries
Mar: GBP 6,000.00 spent, 265 enquiries
Apr: GBP 8,000.00 spent, 240 enquiries
May: GBP 5,000.00 spent, 230 enquiries

Which of these claims does the data contradict?
options: A. Enquiries rose every time spend rose from one month to the next
B. The month with the lowest spend also had the fewest enquiries
C. Enquiries were above 200 in four of the five months
D. Spend doubled between February and March
E. The best month for enquiries cost less than GBP 7,000 in advertising
questions.explanation: Spend rose from GBP 6,000.00 in Mar to GBP 8,000.00 in Apr, and enquiries fell from 265 to 240. That one pair is enough to contradict the claim, and Apr is also the heaviest month of spending in the table for the second-best return. The other four statements all hold against the figures.

questions.prompt:
Seven readings, in order: 11, 14, 14, 20, 23, 26, 32

Which statement about these readings is accurate?
options: A. The mean is greater than the median
B. The mode is greater than the median
C. The range is smaller than the mean
D. The mean and the median are equal, and the mode is below both
E. The mean and the mode are equal
questions.explanation: The seven readings total 140, so the mean is 20, and the fourth value makes the median 20 as well. The repeated 14 sits below both. The range is 21, which is larger than the mean, not smaller.

questions.prompt:
Four chairs and three tables cost GBP 540.00. Two chairs and five tables cost GBP 690.00.

Select the price of one chair AND the price of one table.
options: A. GBP 120.00 a chair; GBP 45.00 a table
B. GBP 45.00 a chair; GBP 120.00 a table
C. GBP 60.00 a chair; GBP 100.00 a table
D. GBP 50.00 a chair; GBP 110.00 a table
E. The two prices cannot be determined
questions.explanation: Doubling the second equation gives four chairs and ten tables for GBP 1,380.00. Subtracting the first leaves seven tables for GBP 840.00, so a table is GBP 120.00 and a chair GBP 45.00. GBP 60.00 and GBP 100.00 satisfy the first equation but not the second, which is why both must be checked.

questions.prompt:
An invoice comes to GBP 1,458.00 including VAT at 20%.

Select the price before VAT AND the amount of VAT in the total.
options: A. GBP 1,166.40 before VAT; GBP 291.60 of VAT
B. GBP 1,458.00 before VAT; GBP 291.60 of VAT
C. GBP 1,215.00 before VAT; GBP 291.60 of VAT
D. GBP 1,215.00 before VAT; GBP 243.00 of VAT
E. GBP 1,200.00 before VAT; GBP 258.00 of VAT
questions.explanation: The total is 120% of the net price, so the net is GBP 1,458.00 / 1.2 = GBP 1,215.00 and the VAT is the remaining GBP 243.00. Taking 20% off the total instead gives GBP 1,166.40, because 20% of the larger figure is not the same as 20% of the smaller one.

questions.prompt:
Staff and leavers last year:

Department One: 340 staff, 51 leavers
Department Two: 90 staff, 18 leavers

Select the department with the higher turnover rate AND the department that lost more people.
options: A. Department One on both measures
B. Department Two on both measures
C. Department One on the turnover rate; Department Two on people lost
D. The two departments are equal on both measures
E. Department Two on the turnover rate; Department One on people lost
questions.explanation: Turnover rates: Department One 15.0%, Department Two 20.0%. People lost: Department One 51, Department Two 18. The smaller department loses a larger share of its staff while the larger one loses more people, so the two measures point in opposite directions.

questions.prompt:
A fund of GBP 40,000.00 grows by 12% a year, compounded annually.

Select the first year-end at which it is worth more than GBP 60,000.00 AND its value at that year-end.
options: A. Year 4; GBP 62,940.77
B. Year 3; GBP 56,197.12
C. Year 5; GBP 70,493.67
D. Year 4; GBP 60,000.00
E. Year 2; GBP 50,176.00
questions.explanation: Year by year: year 1 GBP 44,800.00, year 2 GBP 50,176.00, year 3 GBP 56,197.12, year 4 GBP 62,940.77. Year 3 is still GBP 3,802.88 short, so the fund does not clear GBP 60,000.00 until year 4, when it stands at GBP 62,940.77.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): parcels handled — Depot X 84,000, Depot Y 31,000, Depot Z 126,000

SOURCE 2 (table): complaints received — Depot X 504, Depot Y 217, Depot Z 630

SOURCE 3 (memo): "Audit the depot with the most complaints for every thousand parcels handled."

Which depot is audited?
options: A. Depot X
B. Depot Z
C. Depot Y
D. The three depots are equal
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Complaints per thousand parcels: Depot X 6.0, Depot Y 7.0, Depot Z 5.0. Depot Y is worst and is also the smallest depot. Depot Z draws the most complaints in total, 630, but handles by far the most parcels.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "The average mark rose from 61 to 74 after the new syllabus was introduced."

SOURCE 2 (note): "From this year, candidates predicted below a pass are entered for a different qualification instead."

SOURCE 3 (table): entries fell from 480 to 310.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Much of the rise reflects which candidates were entered rather than the syllabus itself
B. The new syllabus raised every candidate's mark by 13 points
C. The syllabus had no effect on marks
D. A smaller entry always produces a higher average
E. The candidates moved to the other qualification would have passed
questions.explanation: Entries fell by 170, and the note says the candidates removed were the weakest, so the group being averaged changed at the same time as the syllabus. The sources cannot separate the two effects, which rules out both the claim that the syllabus did all the work and the claim that it did none.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): unit price — Supplier A 18.4 euros, Supplier B 21.9 euros, Supplier C 16.75 euros

SOURCE 2 (table): minimum order — Supplier A 500 units, Supplier B 300 units, Supplier C 1,000 units

SOURCE 3 (email): "We need exactly 800 units at the lowest total cost in sterling. The rate is 1.15 euros to the pound."

Which supplier should be used?
options: A. Supplier B
B. Supplier A
C. Supplier C
D. All three cost the same
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Supplier C has the lowest unit price but will not take an order below 1,000 units, so it cannot supply exactly 800. Of the two that can, Supplier A costs GBP 12,800.00 and Supplier B costs GBP 15,234.78, so Supplier A is cheapest. The lowest price per unit is not the lowest price at this volume.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (memo): "Our share of the market fell from 24% to 19% last year."

SOURCE 2 (table): our unit sales rose 8% over the same year.

SOURCE 3 (email): "The board wants to know what happened to our revenue."

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Revenue rose by 8%
B. Revenue fell by 5%
C. Revenue was unchanged
D. The total market shrank
E. Revenue cannot be determined from these sources
questions.explanation: Revenue is units multiplied by price, and no source gives a price or says it held steady, so an 8% rise in units settles nothing about revenue. The sources do fix the direction of the market — units up 8% on a share down from 24% to 19% means the market grew — but that is a different question from the one asked.

questions.prompt:
What is the perimeter of a square?

(1) Its area is 81 square centimetres.
(2) Its diagonal is 9 times the square root of 2 centimetres.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1) the side is the square root of 81, which is 9, so the perimeter is 36 cm. From (2) the diagonal of a square is the side times the square root of 2, so the side is again 9 and the perimeter again 36 cm. The two statements agree, and either alone is enough.

questions.prompt:
For how many hours did a machine run yesterday?

(1) It produced 480 units.
(2) It was switched on from 07:30 to 16:00, with a single 30-minute stoppage.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives output but no rate, so the hours could be anything. (2) covers 8 hours 30 minutes of elapsed time less the 30-minute stoppage, which is exactly 8 hours of running. Only the second statement fixes the figure; the first would need a units-per-hour rate to be of any use.

questions.prompt:
What is a fund worth at the end of its first year?

(1) It started the year at GBP 12,000.
(2) It grew by 7% over the year.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives the starting figure but no growth, and (2) gives the growth but no starting figure, so neither alone reaches a value. Together, GBP 12,000 multiplied by 1.07 is GBP 12,840. Both statements are needed and both are used.

questions.prompt:
Is the average of four numbers greater than 20?

(1) Two of the numbers are 18 and 26.
(2) The other two numbers are each greater than 10.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: The two named numbers total 44. If the other two are 11 and 12 the average is 16.75, which is not above 20; if they are 40 and 50 the average is 33.5, which is. Both cases satisfy (1) and (2) together, so even combined the statements leave the answer open.

questions.prompt:
Which library lends the most books for each hour it is open?

Library | Staff | Annual loans | Opening hours a week | Members
Aldwych | 9 | 74,000 | 30 | 5,000
Boughton | 4 | 21,000 | 30 | 2,100
Chalfont | 14 | 138,000 | 62 | 9,000
Dunmow | 7 | 46,000 | 40 | 4,400
Elverton | 11 | 96,000 | 55 | 6,300
Fairwood | 5 | 33,000 | 34 | 2,900
options: A. Aldwych
B. Chalfont
C. Dunmow
D. Elverton
E. Fairwood
questions.explanation: Annual loans divided by weekly opening hours: Aldwych 2,467, Boughton 700, Chalfont 2,226, Dunmow 1,150, Elverton 1,745, Fairwood 971. Aldwych is highest at about 2,467, because it lends heavily over unusually short hours. Chalfont lends the most books in total but stays open more than twice as long to do it.

questions.prompt:
How many libraries lend more than 14 books a year for each member on their roll?

Library | Staff | Annual loans | Opening hours a week | Members
Aldwych | 9 | 74,000 | 30 | 5,000
Boughton | 4 | 21,000 | 30 | 2,100
Chalfont | 14 | 138,000 | 62 | 9,000
Dunmow | 7 | 46,000 | 40 | 4,400
Elverton | 11 | 96,000 | 55 | 6,300
Fairwood | 5 | 33,000 | 34 | 2,900
options: A. One
B. Two
C. Three
D. Four
E. Five
questions.explanation: Loans divided by members: Aldwych 14.8, Boughton 10.0, Chalfont 15.3, Dunmow 10.5, Elverton 15.2, Fairwood 11.4. Above 14: Aldwych, Chalfont, Elverton — 3 libraries. Size is no guide here: the largest and one of the smallest fall on opposite sides of the line.

questions.prompt:
Which library accounts for more than a quarter of all loans across the six?

Library | Staff | Annual loans | Opening hours a week | Members
Aldwych | 9 | 74,000 | 30 | 5,000
Boughton | 4 | 21,000 | 30 | 2,100
Chalfont | 14 | 138,000 | 62 | 9,000
Dunmow | 7 | 46,000 | 40 | 4,400
Elverton | 11 | 96,000 | 55 | 6,300
Fairwood | 5 | 33,000 | 34 | 2,900
options: A. Aldwych
B. Boughton
C. Elverton
D. Chalfont
E. Fairwood
questions.explanation: The six libraries lend 408,000 books between them, so a quarter is 102,000. Shares: Aldwych 18.1%, Boughton 5.1%, Chalfont 33.8%, Dunmow 11.3%, Elverton 23.5%, Fairwood 8.1%. Only Chalfont clears it; Elverton, the next largest, reaches 23.5%.

questions.prompt:
How many libraries are above the median on both loans per member and weekly opening hours?

Library | Staff | Annual loans | Opening hours a week | Members
Aldwych | 9 | 74,000 | 30 | 5,000
Boughton | 4 | 21,000 | 30 | 2,100
Chalfont | 14 | 138,000 | 62 | 9,000
Dunmow | 7 | 46,000 | 40 | 4,400
Elverton | 11 | 96,000 | 55 | 6,300
Fairwood | 5 | 33,000 | 34 | 2,900
options: A. One
B. Two
C. Three
D. Four
E. Five
questions.explanation: The median is 13.09 loans per member and 37 opening hours. Above on loans per member: Aldwych, Chalfont, Elverton. Above on opening hours: Chalfont, Dunmow, Elverton. On both lists: Chalfont, Elverton — 2.
